facts.fact: The column says Powertel and Paratus Zimbabwe formed an equal-investment PPP to build a DWDM fibre backhaul network across Zimbabwe delivering up to 10 Tbps of cross-border bandwidth linking Zimbabwe, Botswana and Zambia; it gives no agreement date, so the published date is used.

The column says the Powertel-Paratus network starts with an active 800 Gbps link between Plumtree and Bulawayo; it gives no date for it, so the published date is used, and it names no other country's traffic carried.

The column says TelOne has ongoing backbone capacity expansions along cross-border transit links such as Kazungula to Zambia/Botswana and Beitbridge to South Africa; no date is given, so the published date is used.

systems.platform: terrestrial fibre, 26,000 km in Zimbabwe, linked to Liquid's regional cross-border network

systems.owner: DFA Zimbabwe with BCS Group and Dandemutande
